finance.tariff_rule: 0.8 x propane-equivalent (Site 1 reference: Con Ed steam), fixed

why_not_chosen: Site 1 is feasible but the weaker proposal for this challenge, and the numbers say so. (1) Cost: Manhattan LCOH is $305/MWh against Con Ed steam at $119/MWh, 2.6x the incumbent, so a 0.8x tariff cannot cover cost without large subsidy; Lansing blended phases 1-2 are $106/MWh against propane-equivalent $136/MWh. (2) Carbon: Site 1 avoids MORE CO2 per MWh delivered (0.353 vs 0.227 t/MWh) because steam is a fossil incumbent, so carbon alone does not favour Lansing; Site 1 wins on tonnes per heat-MWh, loses on cost per tonne. (3) Source: legacy air-side cooling gives ~32 C capture; like-for-like COP 5.1 vs 6.0 for liquid cooling at Lansing, and a retrofit cannot specify the cooling architecture. (4) Competition: a Con Edison thermal-network pilot near the same NYCHA housing has been reported but is unverified; if confirmed, a second source would compete with the utility rather than fill a gap. (5) Leverage: Lansing is a new build with a live ban fight, so heat reuse is a decision-changing concession and liquid cooling can be specified from day one.
